learning_outcomes.text: Students will possess advanced knowledge and skills (critical understanding of theories and principles) in the field of modern quantum mechanics with emphasis on the structure of matter and its interaction with electromagnetic radiation.
Students will be able to use the knowledge they acquired in a way that shows a professional approach to their work.

Students will be able to gather and interpret elements of the subject to form scientifically documented opinion, both on scientific and social/ethical issues (e.g., risks of new technologies to human health).

Students will be able to communicate information and solutions to the subject of the course (structure of matter and interaction with electromagnetic radiation) to both a specialized and non-specialized audience.
Students will have developed those knowledge-acquiring skills, which they need to pursue further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Analytical and synthetic ability to solve problems.
Manages complex physical theories and mathematical techniques.

syllabus_topics: Mathematical foundations of quantum mechanics, Hermitian operators, Eigenvalues, continuous and discrete spectrum. Conservation laws.
Dirac formalism, Harmonic oscillator, Angular momentum, Spin, synthesis of spins.
Time-Dependent Problems, Approximation Techniques in Time-Dependent Problems. Laser radiation and interaction with matter.
teaching_methods: Use of ICT in delivery and communication with students
assessment_rules: The grading scheme is either Active participation in the class (10%), Homework (20%), and Exam (70%), OR a Final Exam (100%). Evaluation methods include problem solving and short-answer questions.
